event_title: Hurricane Polo restricts shipping at Mexican Pacific ports
cause: The Mexican Navy and port captaincies restricted navigation as a precaution against high winds, heavy rain and large waves from Hurricane Polo as it moved slowly north offshore.
cause_attributed_by: Secretaria de Marina and port captaincies, as reported
confidence_note: Closure dates and the Zihuatanejo and Lazaro Cardenas reopenings are consistent across Reuters, trade and Mexican press, but no Secretaria de Marina notice could be retrieved directly. Sources differ on whether Lazaro Cardenas was closed to small or to larger vessels; one weather-risk firm says larger, and a zero call count on 2026-09-23 and 2026-09-24 supports it. Daily port call counts at these ports are small and noisy.
summary: Hurricane Polo, which reached Category 5 strength offshore of southwestern Mexico on 2026-09-22 (22 September 2026), led the Mexican Navy to restrict navigation at several Pacific ports. Acapulco and Zihuatanejo were closed to all vessels, while Manzanillo, Lazaro Cardenas, Puerto Marques and Puerto Escondido were closed to smaller vessels or, in one report, larger ones at Lazaro Cardenas. Manzanillo, the country's largest container port, kept handling large ships. Zihuatanejo reopened on 2026-09-25 after three days, and Lazaro Cardenas reopened to larger vessels that afternoon. The storm stayed offshore and did not make landfall in this region, and later closures on the Baja California peninsula are not covered by this record.

event_title: Typhoon Dujuan halts cargo calls at Yokohama and Tokyo Bay ports
cause: Typhoon Dujuan brought high seas, strong winds and record rainfall to the Kanto coast, and the Port of Yokohama suspended operations for 45 hours.
cause_attributed_by: Logistics firms Kuehne+Nagel and SEKO Logistics, as reported
confidence_note: The 45 hour Yokohama closure is reported by two forwarder bulletins that agree with each other and with our port call series, but no statement from the port authority or Japanese government on the port closure could be retrieved, and one source notes no blanket shutdown of Tokyo and Yokohama container terminals, so the exact scope of terminal closures is uncertain.
summary: Typhoon Dujuan passed close to the Kanto region of Japan on 2026-09-21 (21 September 2026), bringing record rainfall, flooding and landslides. Kuehne+Nagel reports that the Port of Yokohama was closed for 45 hours from 2026-09-20 to 2026-09-22. Our port call series shows Yokohama, Tokyo, Kawasaki and Chiba falling to near zero daily calls on 2026-09-20 and 2026-09-21 and returning to normal levels on 2026-09-22. The closure was followed straight away by national holidays on 2026-09-21 to 2026-09-23, so yards stayed full and vessel waits at Yokohama reached 1.5 to 2 days.

event_title: Typhoon Saudel closes Ningbo and Shanghai container terminals
cause: Port operators suspended terminal work under typhoon emergency responses activated by local authorities as the storm approached the Zhejiang and Fujian coast.
cause_attributed_by: Ningbo and Shanghai port authorities and terminal operators, as reported by logistics firms
confidence_note: Closure and reopening times come from a carrier advisory and forwarder notices that agree with each other and with our port call series, but no statement from a port authority was retrieved.
summary: Typhoon Saudel stopped container handling at Ningbo-Zhoushan and Shanghai in late August 2026, about two weeks after Typhoon Dolphin. Ningbo suspended empty container work from 16:00 on 2026-08-26 (26 August 2026) and all terminal operations that evening, with roughly 800 vessels reported moved to safe anchorages. Yangshan halted on 2026-08-27 (27 August 2026) and Waigaoqiao suspended empty container work the same day. Saudel came ashore in southern Zhejiang around midday on 2026-08-28 (28 August 2026), and terminals at Waigaoqiao, Yangshan and Ningbo reopened between midday and 15:00 that day. Forwarders warned that bunched arrivals would add to congestion already present across North Asia.

event_title: Typhoon Dolphin halts container terminals at Ningbo and Shanghai
cause: Terminal operators suspended gate and berth operations ahead of the typhoon after China's National Meteorological Center and flood control authorities issued warnings and emergency responses for Zhejiang and Fujian.
cause_attributed_by: Terminal operators and Chinese weather authorities, as reported by logistics firms
confidence_note: Dates rest on freight forwarder and carrier advisories that agree with each other and with our port call series, but no statement from Ningbo-Zhoushan Port or Shanghai International Port Group was retrieved. The stranded capacity figure is a third-party estimate quoted by one source.
summary: Typhoon Dolphin shut container handling at Ningbo-Zhoushan and Shanghai in early August 2026. Terminals at Ningbo suspended empty and laden container gate operations from 2026-08-07 (7 August 2026), and the Yangshan and Waigaoqiao terminals at Shanghai followed on 2026-08-08 (8 August 2026), ahead of a landfall in Zhejiang province on 2026-08-09 (9 August 2026). Ningbo terminals restarted on the afternoon of 2026-08-10 and Shanghai early on 2026-08-11. Ships had sheltered outside the anchorages and returned together, so waiting times of several days and carrier port omissions followed for weeks, and one carrier-side estimate put stranded capacity above 2.4 million TEU. Our port call series show Ningbo and Shanghai logging zero or near zero calls on the closure days.

event_title: River pilots stop work on the Parana corridor in Argentina
cause: Pilots stopped taking new work in protest at Decree 690/2026, which the government said was meant to cut logistics costs and open the profession. Their association cited navigation safety and legal uncertainty over liability.
confidence_note: Four independent outlets agree on the decree, the start on 1 August, the 4 August agreement and the 6 August suspension decree, but ship counts differ (140, more than 150, about 200) and the Official Bulletin text was not retrieved.
summary: Starting on 2026-08-01 (1 August 2026), most river and harbour pilots in Argentina stopped accepting new assignments after a presidential decree, published on 31 July, reformed the rules for pilotage. Large vessels cannot move safely on the Parana waterway without a pilot, so ships could not enter or leave ports. Press counts of waiting vessels ranged from about 140 to more than 150, with grain and fuel shipments held up at the Greater Rosario hub. The coast guard ordered pilots back to work and warned of sanctions. On 2026-08-04 the government and the pilots agreed to suspend the decree, cut pilotage tariffs by 20 percent and open a joint working group. Decree 716/2026, published on 2026-08-06, formalised the suspension.

event_title: Workers strike at Chittagong port over New Mooring Container Terminal lease
cause: Workers opposed the proposed concession of the New Mooring Container Terminal to DP World and also protested transfers of protesting staff.
cause_attributed_by: Chattogram Bandar Rokkha Sangram Parishad, as reported
confidence_note: Dates are consistent across Bangladeshi and trade press, but no official statement from Chattogram Port Authority or the government was retrieved, and the strike was suspended rather than settled, so the end date marks the resumption of work.
summary: Workers and employees at Chittagong (Chattogram), Bangladesh's main seaport, disrupted cargo handling from 2026-01-31 (31 January 2026) to protest a plan to lease the New Mooring Container Terminal to DP World. The action began with eight-hour stoppages on three days, became an indefinite strike from 2026-02-03 (3 February 2026), paused for two days after talks with the shipping adviser, and resumed on 2026-02-08 (8 February 2026). Operations restarted on 2026-02-09 (9 February 2026) after the government said the agreement would not be signed under the interim administration. Reports cited more than 41,000 TEU piled in terminal yards, thousands of export containers held at inland depots, and vessels waiting.

Six highway workers on the bridge were killed. Temporary alternate channels for shallow draft vessels opened in early April, and a limited access channel 300 feet wide and 35 feet deep followed on 2024-04-25. The Army Corps of Engineers and the Navy Supervisor of Salvage and Diving announced on 2024-06-10 (10 June 2024) that the channel had been restored to 700 feet wide and 50 feet deep after about 50,000 tons of wreckage were removed.

cause: Port authorities and terminal operators suspended cargo handling as a precaution before the cyclone reached the Gujarat coast, moving ships out of the Gulf of Kutch and stopping quayside work until damage could be assessed.
cause_attributed_by: Deendayal Port Authority and Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone, as reported

summary: Cyclone Biparjoy suspended cargo handling at ports along the Gulf of Kutch in Gujarat, India, from 2023-06-12 (12 June 2023), ahead of a landfall near Jakhau on 2023-06-15 (15 June 2023). Mundra, India's largest container port, stopped work on 2023-06-12, and Deendayal Port at Kandla suspended all cargo operations and told inbound ships to stay in open water rather than approach the Gulf of Kutch. Berthing schedules and landside container flows at Mundra stayed disrupted afterwards, and trade bodies expected recovery within about a week.

event_title: Drought cuts draft and daily transits at the Panama Canal
cause: The Panama Canal Authority attributed the restrictions to an extended dry season, high evaporation and rainfall well below average in the canal watershed, which lowered Gatun Lake, the fresh water source for the locks. It cited the lowest recorded October rainfall since 1950 and forecast El Nino conditions.
cause_attributed_by: Panama Canal Authority
confidence_note: Every draft figure, transit limit and date comes from dated Panama Canal Authority advisories to shipping and the authority's own statements.
summary: From 2023-03-01 (1 March 2023) the Panama Canal Authority cut the maximum authorised draft in the Neopanamax locks below its normal 15.24 m (50 feet), the first of a series of reductions caused by low water in Gatun Lake. The draft fell in steps to 13.41 m (44 feet) during June 2023, and from 2023-07-30 (30 July 2023) the authority also limited daily transit capacity to an average of 32 vessels. After the driest October in its records, the authority cut booking slots to 25, then 24, then 22 a day in December 2023, and scheduled further cuts to 20 and 18 that it later cancelled. Rain from late 2023 allowed 24 slots a day from 2024-01-16. The draft returned to 15.24 m on 2024-08-15 and 36 daily booking slots resumed for transit dates from 2024-09-01.

event_title: Earthquake and container fire close Iskenderun port in Turkey
cause: Maersk attributes the closure to severe structural damage from the earthquake of 2023-02-06 and the fire among containers that followed. None of the sources reviewed gives an official account of how the fire started.
cause_attributed_by: A.P. Moller - Maersk
confidence_note: The closure and diversion rest on Maersk's own advisories and Reuters reports of the defence ministry and maritime authority. Reopening was staged over several months and carriers give different dates, so the end date marks only the first partial reopening.
summary: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake on 2023-02-06 (6 February 2023) damaged the port of Iskenderun in southern Turkey and set stacked containers on fire. Maersk said the port suffered severe structural damage and all operations stopped, and Turkey's maritime authority told ships to use other ports. The defence ministry said on 2023-02-07 that military aircraft had put the fire out; it flared again and was contained that night. Carriers sent cargo to Mersin, which became congested. Kuehne+Nagel reported that one Limak berth would reopen in early April using mobile cranes, and Maersk made its first trial call during the week of 2023-04-10 (10 April 2023). Maersk kept bookings to the port closed pending further trials.

event_title: Cargo truckers strike cuts container movement at South Korean ports
cause: The union struck to keep the Safe Rates system, which sets minimum haulage rates for container and cement trucking and was due to expire at the end of 2022, to remove its sunset clause and to extend it to more freight types. The government said removing the sunset clause was not possible, and the opposition passed a committee bill to extend the system by three years while the governing party said the question should wait until drivers returned.
cause_attributed_by: Cargo Truckers Solidarity Union and the Korean government
confidence_note: The start date and the union's demands come from the International Transport Workers' Federation, the federation of the striking union. The return to work orders, the port throughput figures and the closing vote rest on Korean press reporting of Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport data, consistent across two outlets, rather than on a ministry release we could retrieve.
summary: From 2022-11-24 (24 November 2022) members of the Cargo Truckers Solidarity Union stopped hauling freight in South Korea, cutting container movement through Busan, Gwangyang, Incheon and Ulsan for 16 days. The union sought to keep and widen the Safe Rates system, minimum haulage rates for container and cement trucking that were due to lapse at the end of 2022. The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport reported that container movement at the country's 12 main ports fell to 37 percent of normal levels on 2022-11-29. The government issued return to work orders, first for cement haulage and then on 2022-12-08 for steel and petrochemical haulage. Members voted on 2022-12-09 (9 December 2022) to end the action, with nearly 62 percent of those voting in favour, and trucks returned the same day. The dispute over the Safe Rates system was not settled.

event_title: Low water closes two stretches of the Lower Mississippi River to barge traffic
cause: The Coast Guard attributed the groundings and closures to low water levels on the Lower Mississippi River. NOAA linked the low water to drought conditions across the basin.
cause_attributed_by: U.S. Coast Guard
confidence_note: The restriction, closure and reopening are reported by the Coast Guard through two press carriers and a Reuters report, but the Coast Guard's own bulletins were not retrieved and the exact reopening day within the weekend of 2022-10-08 to 2022-10-09 is not stated.
summary: Falling water in the Lower Mississippi River led to barge groundings and, on 2022-10-04 (4 October 2022), a Coast Guard waterway restriction near Stack Island, Mississippi, and a closure at Memphis, Tennessee. The Coast Guard set up a recovery unit with agency and industry partners the next day. Queues grew to more than 100 tow boats at the two sites. Dredging deepened the channel, and on 2022-10-10 the Coast Guard said both stretches had reopened over the preceding weekend, with one-way traffic and limits on barge draft and tow size still in force. NOAA counted 144 vessels and 2,253 barges backed up during October, and the river at Memphis fell to a record low on 2022-10-17.

cause: Port and shipping operations were suspended because of Typhoon Muifa, which crossed Zhoushan Island and came ashore in Shanghai on 2022-09-14 and 2022-09-15.

event_title: Live fire exercise zones around Taiwan divert shipping
cause: The Eastern Theater Command said the exercises were a response to what it called an escalation by the United States on the Taiwan question and a warning against moves towards Taiwanese independence.
cause_attributed_by: People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command

summary: From noon on 2022-08-04 (4 August 2022) the People's Liberation Army held live fire exercises in zones around Taiwan, and merchant ships were told to keep clear of the water and airspace involved. The Eastern Theater Command announced the operations on 2022-08-02 (2 August 2022) after a visit to Taipei by the Speaker of the United States House of Representatives, and named areas off the northern, southwestern and southeastern coasts of the island as well as long range firing in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan's transport ministry told vessels to avoid the zones, several of which lay near commercial ports including Kaohsiung. Traffic inside the zones thinned on the first day and ships routed around the eastern side of the island. The announced windows ran to noon on 2022-08-07, and the command said on 2022-08-10 (10 August 2022) that it had finished.

summary: Between 2022-06-09 (9 June 2022) and 2022-07-16 (16 July 2022) the union ver.di called three warning strikes at German North Sea ports during a pay round covering about 12,000 port workers. After a sixth round of talks with the Zentralverband der deutschen Seehafenbetriebe ended without agreement, ver.di called a 48 hour stoppage from 06:00 on 2022-07-14 to 06:00 on 2022-07-16 at Hamburg, Bremerhaven, Bremen, Wilhelmshaven, Emden and Brake, the longest such action at these ports in decades. A settlement before the Hamburg labour court paused further action, and the two sides agreed terms on 2022-08-23.

event_title: Shanghai COVID-19 lockdown restricts trucking to the port
cause: The restrictions were COVID-19 control measures ordered by the Shanghai city government during an Omicron outbreak, lifted when the city said the outbreak had been brought under control.
cause_attributed_by: Shanghai Municipal People's Government

summary: Shanghai began a staged COVID-19 lockdown on 2022-03-28 (28 March 2022), starting in Pudong and extending to the rest of the city from 2022-04-01, and lifted citywide restrictions on 2022-06-01 (1 June 2022). The container terminals at Yangshan and Waigaoqiao kept working under closed loop arrangements, and the carrier Maersk reported in early April that terminal operations continued without delay. The restriction fell on the landside: trucking capacity into and out of the city was cut by driver shortages, testing and quarantine rules, and warehouses inside locked down areas stopped work. Carriers shifted boxes to barge and rail and omitted some calls. The city said normal production and daily life would resume from 2022-06-01, and trade press reported container work close to normal levels in early June.

event_title: Ukraine's Black Sea ports close to commercial shipping after the invasion
cause: Ukrainian authorities suspended commercial shipping at the country's ports after Russia's invasion on 2022-02-24, and Russia closed the Azov Sea to commercial vessels, as reported by Lloyd's List and Ship Technology.
cause_attributed_by: Ukrainian authorities as reported by Lloyd's List and Ship Technology
confidence_note: The resumption dates and the corridor movements are confirmed by United Nations sources, while the start of the closure rests on trade press reporting from 2022-02-24 and 2022-02-25 rather than a Ukrainian government document.
summary: From 2022-02-24 (24 February 2022) commercial shipping stopped at Ukraine's Black Sea and Azov Sea ports after Russia's invasion, and merchant ships and their crews were left in port. The International Maritime Organization Council met in extraordinary session on 2022-03-10 and 2022-03-11 and agreed to encourage a blue safe maritime corridor so that ships and seafarers could leave the area. Grain exports restarted under the Black Sea Grain Initiative, signed in Istanbul on 2022-07-22, with the first outbound vessel leaving Odesa on 2022-08-01 (1 August 2022). The United Nations said it was the first cargo ship to leave a Ukrainian Black Sea port since 2022-02-26. Movements at Chornomorsk and Pivdennyi followed in August 2022. Mariupol, under Russian control, did not reopen to commercial traffic.

event_title: Floods cut both rail lines and the highways serving the Port of Vancouver
cause: The port authority attributed the disruption to widespread flooding in Metro Vancouver, the Fraser Valley and the British Columbia interior, which damaged rail and road infrastructure. Canadian Pacific attributed its damage to the atmospheric river storm that began on 2021-11-14.

summary: Flooding and mudslides after an atmospheric river storm that began on 2021-11-14 (14 November 2021) damaged the railways and highways linking the Port of Vancouver to the rest of Canada. On 2021-11-16 the Vancouver Fraser Port Authority said all rail service to and from the port had stopped, because neither CN nor CP could run trains between Kamloops and Vancouver. Trucks kept serving all four container terminals, and demand for ship anchorages neared capacity. British Columbia declared a province-wide state of emergency effective 2021-11-17. Canadian Pacific reopened its line on 2021-11-23 (23 November 2021) and trains from both railways used it, while CN expected its own line to open on 2021-11-25.

event_title: Hurricane Ida closes New Orleans and the Lower Mississippi River
cause: The Coast Guard closed the river to vessel movement ahead of Hurricane Ida, which made landfall in Louisiana on 2021-08-29. Reopening waited on the removal of power lines from a transmission tower that fell across the waterway near mile marker 106.5 and on a survey of the ship channel.
cause_attributed_by: U.S. Coast Guard
confidence_note: The closure and the reopening are documented by the Coast Guard, but the Coast Guard bulletin and the port release give different days for the river reopening, so the end date follows the bulletin that describes the removal of the obstruction.
summary: From 2021-08-28 (28 August 2021) the Captain of the Port set port condition Zulu before Hurricane Ida and prohibited vessel movement on the Lower Mississippi River, closing the Port of New Orleans and the other river ports of southeast Louisiana. Ida made landfall in Louisiana on 2021-08-29 as a category 4 hurricane. A downed transmission tower dropped power lines across the channel near mile marker 106.5 and a survey of the ship channel was required before traffic could return. The Coast Guard reopened the river to all vessel traffic on 2021-09-03 (3 September 2021), with speed and tow size limits between mile markers 108 and 167.5. The port resumed limited cargo work on 2021-09-02 and container operations on 2021-09-07.

event_title: Typhoon In-fa halts container handling at Shanghai and Ningbo ports
cause: The ports halted ahead of and during Typhoon In-fa, which China's National Meteorological Centre placed under an orange alert and which crossed Zhejiang province on 2021-07-25.
cause_attributed_by: Lloyd's List, Bloomberg and the Yangshan Port Maritime Safety Administration, as reported
confidence_note: Every source is trade or general press and no port authority or maritime safety notice was retrieved. The Yangshan closure rests on a Bloomberg report quoting a social media post and unnamed people, Ningbo is supported only by Lloyd's List and SEKO Logistics through FreightWaves with no times, and no source gives reopening times.
summary: Typhoon In-fa halted container handling at Shanghai and Ningbo in late July 2021. Lloyd's List reported on 2021-07-23 (23 July 2021) that pickups and deliveries were being suspended at terminals in both ports, and said Yangshan would stop box pickups from 06:00 and deliveries from 12:00 on 2021-07-24. On 2021-07-24 the Yangshan maritime safety administration said vessels had been moved out and all terminals had halted. In-fa reached Zhejiang province on 2021-07-25. Bloomberg reported Shanghai's ports shut until at least 2021-07-27, and Lloyd's List said on that date that operations were restarting. No source reviewed gives a reopening time for Ningbo or for individual Shanghai terminals.

event_title: COVID-19 controls cut container handling at Yantian in Shenzhen
cause: The operator attributed the reduced operations to COVID-19 control measures in the port area after cases were found there, and said on 2021-06-23 that the virus was under control and terminal capacity had recovered.
cause_attributed_by: Yantian International Container Terminals
confidence_note: The restriction dates come from the terminal operator's own notice and from a carrier advisory updated through the episode, with consistent trade press reporting. The window does not overlap Lunar New Year or China's National Day holiday exclusions.
summary: Container handling at Yantian in Shenzhen was cut from 2021-05-25 (25 May 2021), after COVID-19 cases were found in the port area, and full operations resumed on 2021-06-24 (24 June 2021). The terminal operator stopped taking laden export containers through the gate late on 2021-05-25, and from 2021-05-26 export and transhipment boxes in the western area were held and operations there stopped. Berths in use fell from 20 to five. Carriers reported the eastern berths running at about 30 percent of normal output in early June, recovering through the month, while about 90 ships skipped Yantian and Shekou. The operator said all berths, including the western area, returned to normal from 00:00 on 2021-06-24, with laden gate in raised to 9,000 trucks a day.

event_title: Winter storm closes Houston, Galveston, Texas City and Corpus Christi ports
affected_places: houston; galveston; texas-city; corpus-christi; freeport-us; us
cause: Port Houston said it suspended operations because of record sub-freezing temperatures, and the Port of Corpus Christi cited freezing temperatures, heavy precipitation, fog and gale-force wind. Port Houston said several public terminals also lost power and water.
cause_attributed_by: Port Houston and Port of Corpus Christi Authority
confidence_note: Closure and reopening times for Galveston, Texas City, Houston, Corpus Christi and Freeport come from one Argus report citing the Coast Guard, and the Maritime Executive reported no Coast Guard restriction on 2021-02-16. Port Houston's own statement is undated on the suspension and reopening, so the end date is an upper bound taken from the 2021-02-23 commission meeting.
summary: A severe winter storm disrupted Texas Gulf Coast ports in February 2021. Galveston and Texas City closed to vessel traffic at 19:00 on 2021-02-14 (14 February 2021), and the Corpus Christi pilots stopped boarding ships that day. According to the Coast Guard as reported by Argus, the Port of Houston and Houston Ship Channel closed at 19:30 on 2021-02-16 and reopened at 10:30 on 2021-02-17. Port Houston suspended its eight public terminals for what a trade report called nearly a week, and told its commissioners on 2021-02-23 that all had resumed. The sources reviewed give no reopening time for Galveston, Texas City or Corpus Christi, and one trade report said no Coast Guard navigation restriction was posted on 2021-02-16.

event_title: Iran seizes the tanker Stena Impero in the Strait of Hormuz
cause: Iran said the tanker was held for marine violations, reported to include switching off its tracking equipment and a collision with a fishing vessel. The United Kingdom government rejected that account and said the seizure was unlawful and came after the detention of an Iranian tanker off Gibraltar earlier in July 2019.
cause_attributed_by: Government of Iran; United Kingdom government
confidence_note: The seizure, its location and the shipping security level come from United Kingdom government statements, and the release date from the operator's own statements and consistent reporting.
summary: On 2019-07-19 (19 July 2019) Iranian forces boarded and seized the British flagged product tanker Stena Impero as it passed through the Strait of Hormuz, and took the ship to Bandar Abbas with its 23 crew aboard. The United Kingdom government said the vessel was intercepted in the westbound traffic lane inside Omani territorial waters by fast boats and a helicopter of the Revolutionary Guard, and called the seizure a breach of international law. Iran said the ship had committed marine violations. On 2019-07-22 (22 July 2019) the Department for Transport raised the security level for British flagged shipping to level 3 and advised against all passage through the strait. Seven crew were released in early September, and the ship left Bandar Abbas for Dubai on 2019-09-27 (27 September 2019).
